source_refs.note: Exercise 9.2, Question 3 (book p. 272); the book prints no answers for Exercise 9.2; answers checked with sympy and the solution book

blocks.explanation:
Three \(\tan^{-1}\) terms must add up to a standard angle.
Plan: join the first two with formula (v), then subtract the third with formula (vi).
steps:
Given: \(\tan^{-1}\frac{3}{4} + \tan^{-1}\frac{3}{5} - \tan^{-1}\frac{8}{19}\).
To prove: it equals \(\frac{\pi}{4}\).
Method: combine two terms at a time. Formula (v) \(\tan^{-1}x + \tan^{-1}y = \tan^{-1}\frac{x+y}{1-xy}\) for the sum, then formula (vi) \(\tan^{-1}x - \tan^{-1}y = \tan^{-1}\frac{x-y}{1+xy}\) for the difference.

Add the first two terms
\[\tan^{-1}\tfrac{3}{4} + \tan^{-1}\tfrac{3}{5}\]
\[= \tan^{-1}\dfrac{\frac{3}{4} + \frac{3}{5}}{1 - \frac{3}{4}\cdot\frac{3}{5}}\]
\[= \tan^{-1}\dfrac{27/20}{11/20} = \tan^{-1}\tfrac{27}{11}\]
Why: \(xy = \frac{9}{20} < 1\), so formula (v) holds. Top: \(\frac{15 + 12}{20} = \frac{27}{20}\); bottom: \(1 - \frac{9}{20} = \frac{11}{20}\); the 20s cancel.

Subtract the third term
\[\text{L.H.S} = \tan^{-1}\tfrac{27}{11} - \tan^{-1}\tfrac{8}{19}\]
\[= \tan^{-1}\dfrac{\frac{27}{11} - \frac{8}{19}}{1 + \frac{27}{11}\cdot\frac{8}{19}}\]
Why: formula (vi); its condition \(xy > -1\) holds because both numbers are positive.

Check
\[0.6435 + 0.5404 - 0.3985 = 0.7854\]
\[\tfrac{\pi}{4} \approx 0.7854\ \checkmark\]
Why: the three angles from a calculator (radian mode) give \(\frac{\pi}{4}\).
